source.title: Exploring Superposition and Interference in State-of-the-Art Low-Parameter Vision Models
source.authors: Lilian Hollard; Lucas Mohimont; Nathalie Gaveau; Luiz Angelo Steffenel

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies SoLU to bottleneck architectures and measures accuracy changes and feature-map alignment as indirect tests of reliance on interference. It does not use the original toy-model setup.
record.gate_note: The paper measures interference-related feature-map directions and the effects of SoLU, so those findings are recorded under V1. It does not measure feature sparsity, count features relative to dimensions, allocate dimensions by feature importance, or compare one-dimensional with multidimensional features. ImageNet scaling and accuracy comparisons are not rows unless they report a feature-alignment or interference result. Values available only in figures are not transcribed as numbers.
record.test_reason: The study borrows superposition and interference as framing for CNN bottleneck design. It does not measure superposition as any version defines it. Its two measures are accuracy loss when SoLU is inserted, which is an intervention effect with no rate of superposition, and Oij, a pairwise alignment of channel feature maps. Neither establishes features outnumbering dimensions, sparsity, a phase transition, polysemantic neurons, or 1-D versus multi-D features. The subjects are vision CNNs, not toy models or LLMs, so V1 and V4 do not apply as named. The interpretation that accuracy loss means 'reliance on interference' is assumed, not shown. The deliverable is the authors' own NoDepth architecture and its scaling.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also claim that BN MobileNeXt and MobileNetv2/v3 scale poorly at low parameter counts because they rely on interference. They claim Batch Norm amplifies interference. They report that their NoDepth Bottleneck scales better than MobileNetv2/v3 on ImageNet. The causal link to superposition is asserted, not demonstrated.
record.recipe_differences: Uses convolutional vision bottlenecks and SoLU interventions with feature-map alignment and accuracy measurements, rather than the original toy-model setup of sparse features competing for dimensions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect changes with bottleneck architecture and normalization choice (Batch Norm versus Layer Norm).

fits_no_version.finding: Inserting SoLU into the residual stream cuts CIFAR-10 accuracy by about 50% for Inverted Bottlenecks and 42% for BN MobileNeXt. The drop is about 1–6% for ConvNeXt-like blocks and 4% for LN MobileNeXt or Sandglass.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sensitivity of vision bottleneck architectures to a superlinear activation (SoLU) depends on block design and normalization (Batch Norm versus Layer Norm).

fits_no_version.finding: Pairwise alignment (Oij) of channel feature maps differs by architecture. MobileNetv3 is mostly 0–0.5, and over half of MobileNeXt-BN layers show aligned maps. SoLU changes alignment in BN models but not in ConvNeXt, LN MobileNeXt or NoDepth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Channel feature-map alignment in CNN bottlenecks varies with architecture and responds to SoLU in BN-based designs.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates or statistical tests are stated. Feature-alignment findings are largely qualitative, and the paper does not report feature sparsity or the number of features relative to available dimensions. The stated Oij interpretation and vector-normalization description do not establish that the measured directions correspond to the sparse features in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: ImageNet accuracy and scaling comparisons are omitted because they do not measure feature alignment or interference. Figure-only numeric values are not transcribed where the text provides no number.
record.verdict_notes: The paper's wording on alignment is inconsistent. The intro says SoLU-affected models use 'non-natural' spaces, while the conclusion says 'dissimilar high-dimensional spaces'. It also says SoLU makes MobileNetv3 align more but pushes MobileNeXt to suboptimal spaces. No uncertainty, seeds or statistical tests are reported, and alignment results are figure-based and qualitative. It cites Toy Models and the SoLU work only as background.

versions.untested_parts: Tests interference-related alignment in vision bottlenecks, but not sparse features exceeding available dimensions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry in the toy-model setting.

rows.subject: MobileNetv2 and MobileNetv3
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 in the standardized vessel
rows.operation_detail: Train the bottleneck with SoLU in the residual stream and compare it with the base architecture.
rows.measure: Accuracy change relative to base architecture
rows.note: The paper reports this result collectively for the v2 and v3 Inverted Bottlenecks; it does not give separate values for each model.
rows.check: Accuracy drop under SoLU in Inverted Bottlenecks is an intervention effect, not a measure of superposition in a toy model or LLM.

rows.subject: ConvNeXt-like Bottleneck
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 in the standardized vessel
rows.operation_detail: Compare the SoLU implementation with a standard bottleneck using ReLU and Batch Norm.
rows.note: Reported across multiple scaling scenarios; individual settings are not specified.
rows.check: The 6% ConvNeXt (ReLU+BN) accuracy drop under SoLU does not measure features versus dimensions or sparsity.

rows.subject: Inverted Bottleneck
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 in the standardized vessel
rows.operation_detail: Replace Batch Norm with Layer Norm and compare the SoLU implementation with the base architecture.
rows.note: The paper says Layer Norm alone does not account for ConvNeXt's stronger performance with SoLU.
rows.check: The 17% drop for the Layer Norm Inverted Bottleneck is an architecture ablation result, not a superposition measure.

rows.subject: Sandglass Bottleneck
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 in the standardized vessel
rows.operation_detail: Compare the SoLU implementation with the base architecture.
rows.note: The paper reports this result for the Sandglass Bottleneck.
rows.check: The 4% Sandglass loss is an accuracy effect only.

rows.subject: MobileNetv3
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 in the standardized vessel
rows.operation_detail: Measure pairwise alignment of feature-map representation directions in the base architecture.
rows.note: The text describes most feature-map vectors as orthogonal and interprets the values as independent features.
rows.check: Oij is alignment between channel feature maps, not feature directions in a sparse-feature setting. Read from Figure 7, with no baseline or control for what alignment to expect.

rows.subject: MobileNetv3
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 in the standardized vessel
rows.operation_detail: Train the same architecture with SoLU to suppress interference noise and compare feature alignment.
rows.value: The network aligns features more closely
rows.note: No numerical alignment value is stated.
rows.check: Qualitative claim that SoLU increases alignment. No number is given, and the measure cannot show V1's effect.

rows.subject: ConvNeXt
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 in the standardized vessel
rows.operation_detail: Compare feature-map direction organization in the base architecture and its SoLU implementation.
rows.value: Most features are orthogonal; the base and SoLU implementations show the same behavior
rows.note: The paper says SoLU has no impact on ConvNeXt accuracy (1%); the feature-alignment description is qualitative.
rows.check: Qualitative ConvNeXt alignment description. Not a superposition measure.

rows.subject: MobileNeXt
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 in the standardized vessel
rows.operation_detail: Measure feature-map direction organization in the base model.
rows.measure: Share of layers exhibiting feature alignment in similar directions
rows.value: Over 50% of layers exhibit this behavior
rows.note: The paper describes this as use of high-dimensional space by aligning features in similar directions.
rows.check: 'Over 50% of layers' showing aligned channel maps is channel correlation, not evidence of features outnumbering dimensions.

rows.subject: MobileNeXt
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 in the standardized vessel
rows.operation_detail: Apply SoLU and assess its effect on the feature organization of the Batch Norm model.
rows.value: SoLU disrupts the architecture's reliance on interference-based representations
rows.note: The paper characterizes the resulting feature spaces as suboptimal for this design; no numerical alignment value is stated.
rows.check: Qualitative interpretive claim about SoLU disrupting 'interference-based representations', with no measure.

rows.subject: MobileNeXt
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 in the standardized vessel
rows.operation_detail: Replace Batch Norm with Layer Norm and compare the SoLU implementation with the base architecture.
rows.note: The paper contrasts this with a 42% drop with Batch Norm.
rows.check: Accuracy drop only (4% with LN versus 42% with BN).

rows.subject: MobileNeXt
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 in the standardized vessel
rows.operation_detail: Compare feature organization in the base model and the Layer Norm model with SoLU.
rows.value: The network maintained similar high-dimensional feature organization, and SoLU did not significantly disrupt it
rows.note: No numerical alignment value is stated.
rows.check: Qualitative statement with no alignment value.

rows.subject: NoDepth Bottleneck
rows.stage_stated: ImageNet proof of concept; training stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compare feature alignment in the base architecture and its SoLU implementation.
rows.value: Feature alignment remains roughly the same
rows.note: The comparison is qualitative; no alignment values are stated.
rows.check: This is the authors' own proof-of-concept architecture. Its alignment is described only qualitatively from Figure 10, so it is a study-method result rather than a test row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Tested bottleneck architectures and normalization settings
reader_labels.reason: The reported alignment and accuracy effects vary by architecture and normalization: some models show aligned feature directions or substantial SoLU effects, while ConvNeXt and Layer-Norm MobileNeXt show little disruption. The study does not establish the sparse-over-capacity condition in V1 (r1-r12).
